reading.body:
E. D. Accounting Siena in Italy is not a data center; it is an accounting firm whose OpenStreetMap tag reflects a mapping error, not commercial colocation infrastructure.

Accounting practices maintain their own server rooms to support local business and client work. These office closets are functionally distinct from commercial data centers, which provide colocation, power redundancy, cooling infrastructure, and hosted services at scale. The presence of a small IT facility inside an accounting office does not constitute data center capacity available to AI workloads or other customers.

This entry documents a common source of noise in infrastructure surveys: misclassified amenities. OpenStreetMap tags applied without verification can inflate apparent data center inventory in a region. Siena's actual capacity for AI compute, if any exists, lies elsewhere and requires independent verification beyond automated geographic cataloging.
